added_failures_note: unmeasured: the reviewed manifest names no baseline_suite/after_suite gate log (it records its two arms under tests/test_logs), so the added-failure count was not taken; supplemental: the reviewed run's arm logs gate-head.log (7 passed) and gate-existing.log (58 passed) each report no FAILED id, so no test regressed -- the only FAILED line in the run directory is the intentional negative control, reproduced independently in this review.

findings.text: follow-on: the run-queue reader's scale and its 'a blocked thread accrues no run-queue time' premise are not asserted against reality -- test_starved_runnable_body_reports_computing replaces _thread_run_wait_seconds with a stub, and the spin case asserts only that run_seconds is not None (a real read that is about 0 either way), so a unit error in reading /proc/self/task/<tid>/schedstat field 1 would leave all seven tests green; the value is correct as written: schedstat field 1 read as 94349988 on the main thread and the reader returned 0.094 s, and a spinning thread showed a +0.28 s CPU delta against a +0.008 s run-queue delta, confirming a running thread accrues almost no run-queue time.

follow-on: plan section 3's deliverable says a computing timeout gives the CLI command that answers without a deadline, but the repair removes read_plan from _CLI_ANSWER_COMMANDS, so read_plan and edit_plan name no command; the intent -- never point at a command that answers a different read -- is satisfied, and a coordinator may wish to tighten the section's wording to 'for tools that have a CLI counterpart' so the deliverable and the code agree.

item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when names tests/test_mcp_deadline_names_its_cause.py; re-ran it at head f31113525 -- 7 passed EXIT=0 (review-gate-head.log) -- and reproduced the negative control in a scratch tree at that head with _thread_cpu_seconds forced to 0.0, which keeps the spinning case red (1 failed, 6 passed, EXIT=1; review-negative-control.log).
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is that a reckon MCP timeout names whether its abandoned body was computing or waiting; reckon/mcp.py:317 _cause_of_timeout and reckon/mcp.py:393 _run_under_deadline report it from the worker thread's CPU seconds (reckon/mcp.py:261) and run-queue wait (reckon/mcp.py:293) read beside the wall time.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it names the four commits (570b7c40c, 4ecc70307, d620e8394, f31113525), the three gate logs and the negative control; its follow_on that read_plan has no CLI counterpart now matches the diff, which dropped read_plan from the map.
item_verdicts.write_paths: git diff --name-only 4ecc703 f311135 lists reckon/mcp.py, reckon/_mcp_tools.py, tests/test_mcp_deadline_names_its_cause.py and the evidence fragment, every one inside the reviewed manifest's declared paths.

justifications.durability: the spinning case pins the exact mapped command in field and hint (tests/test_mcp_deadline_names_its_cause.py:61-62), the sleeping case pins read_plan carrying none (:76-77), the starved case pins the run-queue verdict and figure (:100-103), and the two readers and _cause_of_timeout are unit-reachable through the module; the sole seam is the starved case replacing _thread_run_wait_seconds with a stub, which is the only way to force deterministic starvation.
justifications.evidence: the gate tests/test_mcp_deadline_names_its_cause.py:48,:65,:80,:119 measures what the done_when asserts; re-ran it at head f31113525 (7 passed EXIT=0, review-gate-head.log) with the six existing reckon.mcp files (58 passed EXIT=0), and reproduced the negative control in a scratch tree with _thread_cpu_seconds forced to 0.0 (review-negative-control.log, 1 failed 6 passed EXIT=1); the run-queue reader's real scale is not asserted anywhere (see the finding on reckon/mcp.py:293).
justifications.fit: the new helpers follow the module's private-reader idiom (reckon/mcp.py:261,293) with no plan or version label; the measure constants are renamed to _COMPUTING_WORK_* to name the combined measure rather than CPU alone; the message builder in reckon/_mcp_tools.py:188 routes both figures through one _timing_fragment helper.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/mcp.py:317 _cause_of_timeout decides computing when the thread's CPU seconds plus its run-queue seconds reach half the wall time (reckon/mcp.py:327), and _run_under_deadline:454 reports it beside waited_seconds, cpu_seconds and run_seconds, leaving the error value storage-slow so no caller's branch changes; the deliverable is met, but a computing timeout now names a CLI command only for roadmap/audit/crew, so that clause holds for only the labels that have a counterpart (see the finding on reckon/mcp.py:334).
justifications.reuse: no existing owner of a thread run-queue reading was found in reckon/ (a search for schedstat finds only this reader), and _timing_fragment replaces the inline CPU fragment rather than sitting beside it; the change reuses the existing baseline/deadline plumbing rather than adding a parallel path.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --name-only 4ecc703 f311135 lists exactly reckon/mcp.py, reckon/_mcp_tools.py, tests/test_mcp_deadline_names_its_cause.py and the evidence fragment, every one inside the manifest's declared write paths, with no plan or shared-index write.
